topSignals.title: Project Jupiter: Environmental group files NM Supreme Court emergency writ to halt September 14 air permit hearing
topSignals.text: — New Energy Economy filed an emergency petition on August 19, 2026 asking the New Mexico Supreme Court to issue a temporary stay and court order halting the September 14 NMED air quality permit hearing for Oracle's Project Jupiter data center (Doña Ana County). The petition alleges due process violations — specifically that the compressed timeline (hearing rescheduled from October to September 14) denies opponents adequate time to investigate technical evidence and prepare their case. If the Court grants the stay, the September 14 milestone slips, further delaying first-power beyond SemiAnalysis's 2029 base case and keeping the 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC deployment in regulatory limbo. Source NM (August 19) | ABQ Journal

topSignals.title: PUCT August 20 (today): ERCOT audit covers 250–300 data center projects — behind-the-meter SOFC explicitly advantaged
topSignals.text: — At today's PUCT open meeting, ERCOT is presenting its good-cause exception request for Batch Zero deadlines, triggered by Governor Abbott's August 3 audit directive. The audit and verification of 250–300 projects (mostly data centers) is expected to take "several months but less than nine months." Truly islanded SOFC facilities with no grid connection fall outside ERCOT's interconnection process entirely, making them the preferred near-term solution for data center operators who cannot wait. Beatty & Wozniak's legal analysis confirms the audit is accelerating interest in behind-the-meter and islanded power solutions. Gibson Dunn | B&W Energy Law | Holland & Knight

topSignals.title: Goldman Sachs: Ceres Power on August European Conviction List — 168% upside forecast
topSignals.text: — Goldman Sachs added Ceres Power (LON: CWR) to its August European Conviction Buy list, framing Ceres as a direct play on AI's power scarcity problem. GS forecasts 168% upside over 12 months, characterizing the July correction (−31%) as a buying window. This is the first major bulge-bracket buy-side endorsement specifically positioning a non-Bloom SOFC licensor as a primary AI infrastructure investment. For Dominic's Ceres-vs-Elcogen tracking: Ceres remains the only European SOFC player with active licensed manufacturing scale. TheStreet / Goldman Sachs

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Torrington expansion to 500 MW/yr announced — FCEL unveiled plans to expand its Torrington, CT manufacturing facility from the previously announced 350 MW/yr target to 500 MW/yr; project cost $200–275M, timeline ~24 months. FCEL also introduced a standardized 12.5 MW modular product for data centers (10 × 1.25 MW modules), reducing repeat engineering and permitting cycles. Q2 2026 sales pipeline grew to 4 GW — a 267% increase from Q1 2026. Backlog $1.14B (down from $1.26B YoY due to revenue recognition). Hartford Business | StockTitan Q2

PUCT August 20 (today) — Batch Zero good-cause exceptions and Abbott audit: See Top Signal #2. ERCOT's exception request covers: (a) missed August 7 large-load classification deadline; (b) August 1 and November 1 quarterly stability assessments; (c) review of 200+ dynamic-data submissions with deficiency notifications. Audit: 250–300 projects, primarily data centers, expected to take several months (<9 months). Fully islanded SOFC installations (no ERCOT interconnection needed) are structurally outside the audit's scope. Behind-the-meter registrations may face new PUCT requirements — watch for post-meeting filings. ERCOT Market Notice M-A080326-01 | Blockspace | Troutman Pepper Locke

NM Supreme Court emergency petition on Project Jupiter (August 19): See Top Signal #1. If the Court issues a temporary stay, the September 14 NMED hearing cannot proceed; the permit decision deadline (November 23) would be missed, delaying the entire permitting track by at least one cycle. Rolls-Royce SMR GDA Step 3 (ONR): August deadline confirmed missed — The 53-month Generic Design Assessment schedule targeted August 2026 for the Design Acceptance Confirmation (DAC). With no DAC issued by ONR as of August 20, the deadline has definitively slipped. ONR has not published a revised timeline. Next expected milestone: Q4 2026 or early 2027. This confirms the SOFC deployment speed advantage in UK/EU markets is maintained through at least 2027. ONR GDA page | World Nuclear News

lcoe.text: FCEL Torrington 500 MW/yr capacity target (new): FCEL's expanded manufacturing scale ($200–275M capital investment) confirms a second large-scale SOFC/MCFC production ramp alongside Bloom's 2 GW/yr Fremont. Competitive supply-side growth is structurally deflationary for SOFC capex over the 2027–2029 horizon. FCEL's 12.5 MW standardized product (10 × 1.25 MW modular) reduces project development cost per MW. Watch for FCEL ASP trend in Q3 FY2026 (October). Hartford Business
Rolls-Royce SMR GDA DAC missed (August 2026): UK/EU nuclear regulatory timeline slips confirmed. No material change to LCOE model SMR-vs-SOFC competitive scenario parameters.

NM Supreme Court petition risk (Project Jupiter): If stay granted: Oracle Jupiter 2.45 GW Bloom deployment delayed beyond 2029. Assess sensitivity: what is the model impact if Bloom's largest single announced commitment slips by 12+ months on revenue recognition timing? At $700–800M/GW revenue and current guidance, a 2.45 GW slip pushes ~$1.7–2B of revenue out. LCOE impact: indirect (investor confidence → capex cost of capital).
